content.title: About
content.content: Soy milk is a plant‑based beverage made from soybeans that are ground, cooked, and filtered. The sweetened version contains added sugar or other sweeteners, giving it a pleasant, mild sweetness. It is a popular alternative to cow’s milk for people with lactose intolerance, vegans, and those seeking a lower‑calorie drink.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Commercial soy milk production began in the United States in the 1930s.
Soy milk provides roughly the same amount of protein as cow’s milk (about 3 g per 100 ml).
Sweetened varieties are often fortified with calcium, vitamin D, and vitamin B12.
Soybeans are a source of isoflavones, which are studied for potential heart‑health and hormonal benefits.
In Japan, soy milk is commonly served chilled during the summer months.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Soy protein contains all essential amino acids, making it a valuable protein source for vegetarians and vegans.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Unlike whole cow’s milk, soy milk is primarily composed of polyunsaturated fats, which are heart‑friendly.

items.title: Source of isoflavones
items.content: Isoflavones may support hormonal balance and contribute to reduced risk of osteoporosis.

items.title: Fortified with calcium and vitamins
items.content: Most commercial versions are enriched with calcium, vitamin D, and vitamin B12, helping to replace nutrients typically obtained from dairy.

items.title: Digestive support
items.content: Sweetened soy milk often contains added probiotics that promote a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Soy allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to soy proteins, ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Added sugar content
items.content: Sweetened versions can contain significant amounts of added sugar, which is undesirable for people with diabetes or those monitoring weight.

items.title: Phytates
items.content: Soy contains phytates that can reduce the absorption of certain minerals (iron, zinc) when consumed in excess.

items.title: Genetically modified organisms (GMOs)
items.content: The majority of soybeans grown worldwide are GMO; those avoiding GMOs should look for certified organic options.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sweetened soy milk can be enjoyed straight, added to smoothies, oatmeal, baked goods, coffee, or used as a base for sauces. For extra flavor, consider adding cinnamon, vanilla, or a dash of cocoa.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store an opened carton in the refrigerator and consume within 5‑7 days. Keep unopened packages in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Discard if the milk develops a sour smell or off‑taste.
